deep.reconstruction:
Context: on the previous page Hilbert asks for a three-dimensional analogue of a Riemann surface. The setting is a multi-valued function on 3-space, branched along a closed curve: a 'Riemann space' glued along cut surfaces. The example is a closed curve with one simple knot, almost certainly the trefoil. The branching is of order 2 ('Periode 2'): one small loop around an arc of the curve changes the function, and a second loop restores it. So the monodromy of every meridian is a transposition. The page continues the construction of cut surfaces that make the complement simply connected, which he says is shown by his own model.

(1) Cut surfaces. A surface spanning the knot is laid through it, bounded only by the curve. A remaining hole is plugged by an extra piece (yellow). This gives 4 surface pieces:
- black s, red r, blue b: these correspond to the three arcs of a trefoil diagram;
- yellow g: the plug, which meets no branch curve.

(2) Sheets. Hilbert says three function branches u, v, w (sheets) are needed. In modern terms this is a 3-sheeted branched cover of S^3 along the knot.

(3) Gluing relations. The subscript w seems to mean 'the value on the near (reference) side'; the subscript s, r, b, g means the value across the piece of that colour.
- Red: u_w = v_r (Periode 2). Read with the next page (U_w=V_r, U_r=V_w, W_w=W_r), red carries the transposition (u v).
- Black: w_w = v_s (Periode 2), i.e. (v w), with u unchanged.
- Blue: w_w = u_b (Periode 2), i.e. (u w), with v unchanged.
- Yellow: u_w = w_g and v_w = u_g (not period 2). Completing it [mine]: w_w = v_g. So yellow carries a 3-cycle.

The three distinct transpositions on the three arcs are exactly a surjective representation of the trefoil group onto S_3 (Wirtinger generators to transpositions), i.e. a Fox 3-colouring. The cover is the irregular 3-fold dihedral branched cover. The plug carries the product of two transpositions, a 3-cycle, as the cocycle condition around the hole requires [my interpretation].

(4) Extent of the red piece. On the red piece only u and v are interchanged; the other function stays unchanged and hence continuous there. The relation u_w = v_r must therefore persist as far as one can continue without crossing another cut surface. So the red piece is extended as far as the model indicates. This is an analytic-continuation argument that fixes the shape and extent of each cut piece.

The next page goes on to define two 'genera' p_1 and p_2 by the number of cuts needed to make closed surfaces, respectively closed curves, contractible (Betti-number-like invariants). It then poses a 3-dimensional generalisation of Riemann's existence theorem: does every prescribed branching scheme come from an algebraic object?
errors: The claim that 3 functions are necessary is not justified as stated. Period-2 branching along any knot is already realised by the 2-sheeted cyclic cover, with every piece swapping u and v and the plug trivial. Three sheets are needed only if one wants distinct transpositions on the three arcs (the dihedral cover), or because of the chosen plug.

The next page's yellow line, as corrected (U_w = U_g and V_w = U_g), does not define a permutation: U_g occurs twice. This page's version (u_w = w_g, v_w = u_g, hence w_w = v_g, a 3-cycle) is the consistent one.
The surface 'bounded only by the curve' that nevertheless leaves a hole needing a plug is described only through the physical model. The geometry cannot be checked from the text.

results.what: Construction of a 3-dimensional 'Riemann space': a branched cover of 3-space along a knotted curve (trefoil) with branching of order 2, built from cut surfaces with sheet-gluing rules
results.modern_name: Branched covering of S^3 along a knot; Seifert-type cut surfaces

results.what: Assignment of the three transpositions (uv), (vw), (uw) to the three arc pieces and a 3-cycle to the plug: a consistent S_3 monodromy of the trefoil
results.modern_name: Dihedral (Fox 3-colouring) representation of the trefoil group; irregular 3-fold dihedral branched cover
results.usually_credited_to: Wirtinger (1905) for monodromy of knot groups; Reidemeister/Fox (1930s-1950s) for dihedral covers and colourings

results.what: Extent of a cut surface fixed by continuing a gluing relation until another cut is met

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains an explicit 3-sheeted cover branched along the trefoil, with transposition monodromy on the arcs and a 3-cycle on the plug, built on a physical model. This is the dihedral cover of the trefoil. If the notebook predates or is contemporary with Heegaard (1898) and Wirtinger (1905), it is a notable unpublished early instance of knot-theoretic branched covers in Hilbert's hand. It is known, however, that the Riemann-space programme was discussed in this circle, the treatment is heuristic, and the date and authorship (lecture notes versus Hilbert's own) are uncertain.

checkable.sympy: from sympy.combinatorics import Permutation; a=Permutation(0,1,size=3); b=Permutation(1,2,size=3); a*b*a == b*a*b
checkable.asserts: The transpositions red=(u v) and black=(v w) satisfy the trefoil braid/Wirtinger relation aba=bab.

checkable.sympy: from sympy.combinatorics import Permutation; a=Permutation(0,1,size=3); b=Permutation(1,2,size=3); a*b*a**-1 == Permutation(0,2,size=3)
checkable.asserts: Conjugating black by red gives the blue transposition (u w), so the three arc colours are consistent with the Wirtinger relations.
The plug (yellow) monodromy, a product of two distinct transpositions, is a 3-cycle (not period 2), as the page states.
The monodromy group generated by the arc transpositions is all of S_3, so the 3-sheeted cover is connected.

transcription_corrections: Line 'u_w = v_r (nicht Periode 2': the image looks like '(mit Periode 2'. This is consistent with red being a transposition on the next page; the 'nicht Periode 2' that follows belongs to the yellow relation u_w = w_g.
Line 'Für die 3 Funktionen u, v, w gelten an den Schnittflächen ...' is correct; the subscript in 'v_s' is s (schwarz).
The transcription is otherwise accurate: 'roth', 'nothwendig', 'Model' (sic), 'angiebt' are period spellings.
